licensure.disciplinary_grounds.rationale: These nine buckets cover the full distribution by separating the dominant clusters: licensing fraud, criminal history, substance-use impairment, clinical skill failures, broad unprofessional conduct, mental/physical fitness, drug-specific diversion or misuse, administrative and reporting duties, and out-of-state discipline—each cluster appearing heavily across many states.

profession_specific.license_tiers.rationale: The data clusters naturally into the two core RN/LPN tiers, a broad APRN umbrella, its four named specialty roles (NP, CRNA, CNM, CNS), paraprofessional nurse aide and medication aide tracks, short-term temporary/interim permits, the Nurse Licensure Compact multistate credential, and a residual bucket for outliers like volunteer licenses, public health nurses, forensic nurses, nursing home administrators, and unlicensed assistive persons.

profession_specific.aprn_role_categories.rationale: All items fall into exactly the four canonical APRN role categories recognized by NCSBN (NP, CRNA, CNM, CNS) plus a residual bucket for states that use a single undifferentiated APRN designation rather than listing individual roles.

profession_specific.lpn_supervision_requ.rationale: The data clusters tightly into named supervisor types—RN and APRN (nursing), Physician and PA (medicine), Dentist (dental), Podiatrist (foot medicine), Optometrist/Chiropractor (less-common allied health), and a small residual group of broad statutory catch-alls—covering every item without overlap.

profession_specific.controlled_substance.rationale: The vast majority of items are discrete DEA schedule designations (II through V), but Schedule II frequently appears with state-specific restrictions (supply limits, patient type, drug class, or collaborative agreement requirements) that warrant a separate bucket, while a handful of states grant authority via a single blanket or combined-schedule statement rather than enumerating schedules individually.
